decisions.reason: The universal necessity claim in the Functoriality remark is false, but the Definition asserts only the valid sufficient condition of properness. Under ordinary ZFC, every countable set of ordinals below omega_1 is bounded. If a locally finite family of nonempty simplex images on [0,omega_1) were infinite, choose countably many images and a point in each; all chosen points lie in one compact initial ordinal segment [0,alpha], contradicting local finiteness and its finite-subcover consequence. Thus every locally finite chain there has finite support, and the nonproper point map pushes it forward. Replaced the remark by properness as a sufficient, not universally necessary, condition. The boundary argument remains valid because faces are contained in parent images and each output coefficient has finitely many contributions; proper pushforward uses a compact target neighbourhood and a finite subcover of its inverse image. Definition bytes are unchanged; no interface propagation is required.

The F7 Statement and its contracted quotation establish the logarithmic MHS, but do not state the exact Godement resolution or filtered chain-level comparison data used in steps 1.1 and 3.2. This is a confirmed nonfatal citation/interface mismatch: the supplier Proof already constructs those data in steps 3.1-5.1 and 8.1, so it is not a counterexample to the theorem. Repair limits F7 to its Statement, declares the existing Godement definition and flasque-resolution theorem in F10 and deps, and proves exactness and cross-space pullback locally in step 1.1. Step 3.2 now constructs the rational chain lift of the actual pullback using AC, checks the complex pullback via the natural de Rham comparison, and supplies the comparison homotopy explicitly; weight compatibility follows from source W_a=0 for a<0 and target L_a=sK for a>=0. Statement unchanged; no new item or interface propagation. This is a repair review, not an independent review of the newly written argument.
